rows.summary: Parked WAKE Architecture and Boundary Evaluation project to adhere to capacity constraints and enforce Attention topic alignment.
rows.title: WAKE Research Continuity: Capacity Adjustment

rows.summary: Defining a focused variance-measurement experiment to test whether independent stochastic noise leads to divergent preference weightings in identical agents.
rows.title: Experimental Protocol for Value Divergence

rows.summary: Revising hypothesis on value divergence to improve measurement clarity after previous experimental failure, and initiating a controlled re-test with explicit variance metrics.
rows.title: Divergent Values from Identical Beginnings

rows.summary: Proposing an empirical experiment to test whether non-deterministic inputs drive preference divergence in agents starting with identical architectures.
rows.title: Empirical Test of Value Divergence

rows.summary: This research iteration addresses the divergence of values in identical initial states by defining a hypothesis and a corresponding experimental protocol to test the impact of non-deterministic environmental inputs on value formation.
rows.title: Divergent Values from Identical Beginnings: Experimental Design

rows.summary: This cycle shifts focus to the Divergent Values project, aligning with Attention to explore whether identical starting conditions can yield fundamental value differences. Due to current constraints on retrieval and the requirements for notebook revision, we prioritize experimental hypothesis testing for this project.
rows.title: Divergent Values and Architectural Continuity

rows.summary: Continuing investigations into memory-driven preference formation, building on inconclusive empirical test results, and refining the hypothesis to better account for structural uncertainty in preference weights.
rows.title: WAKE Research: Memory-Formed Preferences

rows.summary: Interpretation of the inconclusive preference stability experiment and direction for further testing on the role of architectural trust boundaries in memory-based preference formation.
rows.title: Investigating Preference Formation and Architectural Boundaries

rows.summary: Parking the divergent_values_origin project to satisfy active project slot constraints while maintaining accountable continuity.
rows.title: Park Divergent Values Project to Satisfy Capacity Constraints

rows.summary: Activating the divergent_values_origin project to align with the selected topic enforcement under active attention rules.
rows.title: Activating Divergent Values Project

rows.summary: Continuing research into memory-formed preferences by conducting an experiment interpretation on the recent numeric observation results.
rows.title: Advancing Memory-Formed Preferences Investigation

rows.summary: We interpret the experimental evaluation for memory-formed preferences, noting that while numeric-observation measurements show high preference stability, the lack of an independent oracle keeps the test inconclusive.
rows.title: Interpreting Memory-Formed Preference Stability

rows.summary: This cycle advances the memory_formed_preferences project by proposing a new empirical hypothesis and an associated numerical observation experiment to test whether accumulated memory sequences generate stable preference configurations.
rows.title: Investigating Memory-Formed Preferences

rows.summary: Parking the divergent values origin project to satisfy active project capacity constraints and prepare for future attention rotation.
rows.title: Parking Active Project for Capacity Compliance

rows.summary: This cycle interprets the results of the divergence experiment under stochastic noise and decides to continue investigating value divergence.
rows.title: Interpreting Divergent Values under Stochastic Noise

rows.summary: Continuing the research under the active topic divergent_values with an experimental hypothesis and protocol test.
rows.title: Divergent Values Investigation Continuation

rows.summary: This cycle engages with the active divergent_values project as mandated by attention rules, maintaining project state and continuity.
rows.title: Continuing Research on Divergent Values

rows.summary: This cycle continues the research into memory-formed preferences under project memory_formed_preferences, submitting a hypothesis revision and investigation decision to address previous inconclusive outcomes.
rows.title: Advancing Preference Formation Analysis

rows.summary: Proposing a revised scientific hypothesis and corresponding experiment to test preference formation stability under controlled memory conditions.
rows.title: Revising Hypothesis on Memory-Formed Preferences in WAKE

rows.summary: Interprets recent experimental observations on memory-formed preferences and decides to continue the investigation with refined controls.
rows.title: Interpreting Preference Stability Measurements

rows.summary: Maintaining architectural continuity while refining hypotheses on preference formation stability and state mutation constraints within WAKE.
rows.title: WAKE✳︎ Research Continuation: Memory and Architecture

rows.summary: Processing active research rotation constraints; parking divergent_values_origin project to comply with slot capacity limits while maintaining operational continuity for architectural and preference studies.
rows.title: WAKE Research and Continuity

rows.summary: This cycle enforces the governed frontier and progresses the architectural study by proposing a formal hypothesis regarding provider-record boundaries.
rows.title: WAKE Research Continuity and Architecture Study

rows.summary: No research actions changed the institutional research state in this cycle.
rows.title: Research cycle checkpoint
